title: ‘You’re very selfish, looking for votes like a retired Almajiri’ — Yesufu attacks Tinubu
description: Activist and politician Aisha Yesufu has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his recent apology to residents of Plateau State, describing him as a “very selfish human being” and accusing him of seeking votes from the people after failing to show concern when they were mourning victims of violence.
content:
Activist and politician Aisha Yesufu has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his recent apology to residents of Plateau State, describing him as a “very selfish human being” and accusing him of seeking votes from the people after failing to show concern when they were mourning victims of violence.

Yesufu made the remarks in reaction to Tinubu’s comments during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Jos on Saturday.

During the rally, the president apologised for not entering Jos during his previous visit to the state following a deadly attack in Angwan Rukuba, Jos North, on April 2, 2026, which reportedly claimed more than 28 lives.

Tinubu had visited Plateau State after the attack but reportedly stopped at Yakubu Gowon Airport in Heipang without proceeding into the town.

Reflecting on the visit during Saturday’s rally, the president said: “When I last visited the other time, I was limited to the airport. Forgive me if you didn’t see me enter the land.”

Reacting in a post on X, Yesufu accused the president of showing little concern for the people during their period of mourning but returning to the state to solicit their votes ahead of the 2027 general election.

“Very selfish human being. You couldn’t be bothered when the people mourned but now go because you are looking for votes like a retired Almajiri,” she wrote.

Her comments followed renewed attention to Tinubu’s previous visit to Plateau State and his explanation for not entering Jos after the April attack.

title: US Airports Expected To Return To Normal Today — Officials
description: US air travel was expected to return to normal on Monday after three days of widespread disruption following an extraordinary no-takeoff order issued by US aviation authorities.The ground stop issued Friday afternoon was only the second time such a directive had been issued nationwide in the busy US
content:
US air travel was expected to return to normal on Monday after three days of widespread disruption following an extraordinary no-takeoff order issued by US aviation authorities.

The ground stop issued Friday afternoon was only the second time such a directive had been issued nationwide in the busy US airspace since planes were grounded following the 9/11 attacks. It was blamed by the Trump administration on a faulty upgrade to communications equipment.

As of Sunday evening, more than 55 US-related flights — those traveling within, into or out of the United States — scheduled for Monday were cancelled, according to industry tracker FlightAware.

That marked a dramatic shift from the more than 1,960 flights cancelled on Sunday.

The Trump administration sought to reassure weary flyers as questions remained over how such chaos could unfold in the world’s largest economy, a country that prides itself on its technological prowess.

Throughout the weekend, stranded passengers wandered through chaotic airports and sat on floors, waiting for updates or to be rebooked.

Officials blamed Friday’s colossal snafu on faulty work to upgrade air traffic control communication cables.

President Donald Trump on Sunday ended uncharacteristic days of silence on the ground stop, but only to blame his predecessor Joe Biden for the debacle.

Trump insisted he inherited a mess from the Biden administration and said Congress, which his party has controlled for two years, must approve funds to upgrade America’s outdated air traffic control system.

“The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster,” Trump said, referring to the Federal Aviation Administration.

“Everything they touched turned bad. Big money spent unwisely, making an old and broken system worse than when they began,” Trump asserted.

FAA chief Bryan Bedford had said Saturday that air travel for millions of Americans stranded at airports would return to normal by the close of business on Sunday.

But Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Sunday morning it will actually take longer to get planes, crews and travelers to where they need to be.

“So, in the airspace, we’re going to see things come back to normal today, but probably fully normal tomorrow,” Duffy said on ABC News.

“We had airplanes and crews out of position because of Friday, so it takes a little bit of time to do that.”

‘I’m The Secretary’

Duffy also flatly rejected calls for his resignation over the travel chaos, insisting he inherited woefully outdated air traffic control infrastructure, such as, he said, radar equipment that dates back to the 1960s.

“So when we do work and things go wrong, of course I’m the secretary. But I also have to acknowledge what was delivered to me,” Duffy said in an interview on CNN.

The ground stop not only plunged US air travel into chaos, it also raised serious concerns about the country’s aging infrastructure.

Duffy has appealed for $50 billion in funds to upgrade and modernize the air traffic control system, and called for Congress, which controls the purse strings of the US government, to “meet this moment.”

But Democrats quickly pounced to say Congress under Trump’s Republicans could already have done this.

AFP

title: ‘Let Tinubu complete his eight years, power will return to North in 2031’ — Bichi appeals to Northerners
description: The Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Appropriations, Rep. Abubakar Bichi, has called on Northerners to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, arguing that political power should return to the region after the president completes his constitutionally permitted second te
content:
The Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Appropriations, Rep. Abubakar Bichi, has called on Northerners to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, arguing that political power should return to the region after the president completes his constitutionally permitted second term.

Bichi said the North should allow the South to complete its eight-year tenure, noting that the region had already enjoyed eight years in power under former President Muhammadu Buhari, while Tinubu had served only four years.

The lawmaker, who represents Bichi Federal Constituency in Kano State, made the appeal in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in Dutse, Jigawa State, on Sunday.

He argued that supporting Tinubu for a second term would allow the South to complete its tenure before power returns to the North.

“What is the magic? We have done our eight years under the late former President Muhammadu Buhari. Now they have done their four years; let them finish so that we can move on.

“Let President Tinubu finish his second term, then power will come back to the North as well. President Tinubu loves the North, and he has done well for the region,” he said.

Bichi also rejected claims that the Tinubu administration had neglected Northern Nigeria, insisting that the region had benefited from several government policies, infrastructure projects and development interventions.

He described the growing support for Tinubu in the North as encouraging, saying the large crowds at All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rallies demonstrated public satisfaction with the administration.

“Contrary to claims in some quarters that Tinubu does not care about the North, the president has demonstrated commitment to the development of the region through major infrastructure and other intervention projects.

“The turnout of people from the North is impressive, and it is a clear testimony that the people are happy with what Tinubu has done so far.

“President Bola Tinubu has performed credibly in the North, and there is no state that has been left out,” he said.

Citing Jigawa State as an example, the lawmaker said Tinubu had approved about ₦80 billion for the Greater Dutse Water Project to address one of the state’s major developmental challenges.

He also highlighted road construction projects in the state, particularly the Kano-Hadejia Road, which he said covers approximately 200 kilometres.

According to him, the Kano-Danja section has been completed, while construction on the Danja-Hadejia stretch is about 80 per cent complete.

Bichi further disclosed that several irrigation projects had been completed in Jigawa, describing them as evidence of the Federal Government’s commitment to infrastructure development and agricultural activities in the North.

“As Chairman of the House Committee on Appropriations, I know what President Tinubu has done in many parts of the North, and it is fantastic,” he said.

He listed Kano, Jigawa, Katsina, Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara among the states that had benefited from the administration’s development initiatives.

The lawmaker expressed confidence that residents of Kano would recognise Tinubu’s contributions to the state, promising to provide further details of projects executed there.

He urged Northerners to reciprocate what he described as the president’s commitment to the region by supporting his administration and acknowledging its achievements.

“It is time for the people of the North to pay back what President Tinubu has done for us,” he said.

Bichi maintained that Tinubu’s performance should be assessed beyond political affiliations, urging residents of the region to support the president’s bid to complete a second term in office.

The post ‘Let Tinubu complete his eight years, power will return to North in 2031’ — Bichi appeals to Northerners appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Airline operators, customs agents, others back Tax Ombud, seek fairer tax system
description: Dr. Allen Onyema, Vice President of the Airline Operators of Nigeria (AON), has applauded the establishment of the Office of the Tax Ombud, describing it as a significant institutional intervention that provides the aviation sector and taxpayers generally with an impartial platform for resolving com
content:
Dr. Allen Onyema, Vice President of the Airline Operators of Nigeria (AON), has applauded the establishment of the Office of the Tax Ombud, describing it as a significant institutional intervention that provides the aviation sector and taxpayers generally with an impartial platform for resolving complaints and addressing grievances.

Delivering a goodwill message at a Town Hall Meeting organised by the Office of the Tax Ombud in Lagos last weekend Onyema highlighted the association’s persistent efforts to draw attention to its grievances at various levels of government, including security and legislative institutions.

Onyema made a strong case for the harmonisation of tax regimes to promote fair competition and sustainability, particularly for private and charter airline operators.

The Tax Ombud/Chief Executive, Dr. John Nwabueze, said the mandate of his Office includes promoting fairness, transparency and accountability in Nigeria’s tax administration system.

He commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, for pioneering the establishment of the Office of the Tax Ombud, which is mandated to address operational, administrative and procedural grievances relating to taxes, levies, regulatory fees and customs duties.

Nwabueze emphasised that the services of the Office are free of charge to Nigerians, providing an impartial platform for resolving disputes through mediation rather than adversarial proceedings.

He further explained that the Office does not determine substantive tax liabilities but focuses on addressing gaps in complaint management and promoting voluntary compliance by building trust between taxpayers and revenue authorities.

Underscoring the importance of stakeholder collaboration involving taxpayers, professional associations, business organisations, civil society and the media, he encouraged participants to share their experiences candidly and offer constructive recommendations.

Nwabueze, who commended the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of Economy, Mr. Taiwo Oyedele, for his leadership in tax reforms, reassured participants of the Office’s independence and commitment to resolving complaints promptly, reiterating its guiding principle of “bridging differences and building trust.”

Engr. Olusola Obadimu, Director-General of the Nigerian Association of Chambers of Commerce, Industry, Mines and Agriculture (NACCIMA), described the Town Hall Meeting as a vital platform for addressing the persistent challenges confronting businesses and industries, ranging from inadequate infrastructure and rising energy costs to the increasing burden of taxation.

Obadimu expressed support for the role of the Tax Ombud and commended Dr. Nwabueze for facilitating open dialogue between government and private-sector stakeholders.

He called on policymakers to prioritise expanding the business landscape and supporting entire economic ecosystems, pledging NACCIMA’s collaboration with the Tax Ombud in promoting an equitable business environment conducive to enterprise growth and national development.

Speaking on behalf of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (ICAN), Mr. Adewale Taju Olayinka emphasised that a fair and trustworthy tax system is fundamental to voluntary compliance and sustainable national revenue generation.

Olayinka welcomed the establishment of the Office of the Tax Ombud as an important step towards strengthening accountability in tax administration and reaffirmed ICAN’s commitment to collaborating with the Office on professional capacity-building and taxpayer education.

Delivering a goodwill message on behalf of the Association of National Accountants of Nigeria (ANAN), Mr. Bernard Akinnola underscored the importance of an equitable and predictable tax system, particularly amid ongoing reforms aimed at strengthening transparency and fiscal sustainability.

He outlined five core principles that ANAN believes should underpin Nigeria’s tax administration system: transparency, equity, respect for taxpayer rights, professionalism and stakeholder collaboration.

Dr. Titilayo Fowokan, speaking on behalf of the President of the Chartered Institute of Taxation of Nigeria (CITN), described the Tax Ombud as a landmark institutional innovation in Nigeria’s tax administration framework, with the potential to strengthen accountability, protect taxpayer rights and promote transparent grievance resolution.

She noted that CITN considers the independent platform essential to building taxpayer confidence and fostering constructive relationships between taxpayers and revenue authorities.

Fowokan reaffirmed CITN’s commitment to supporting the Tax Ombud’s mandate and promoting high professional standards in tax administration.

Speaking on behalf of the Executive Director of the Nigerian Export Promotion Council (NEPC), Arc. Benedict Itegbe commended the Office of the Tax Ombud for extending its stakeholder engagement to Lagos.

He noted that free and impartial mechanisms for seeking redress are crucial to promoting a competitive non-oil export sector.

Itegbe urged exporters to maintain comprehensive records and take advantage of the avenues provided by the Tax Ombud to address complaints relating to unfair treatment and complex tax-compliance challenges.

He assured the Office of NEPC’s readiness to promote awareness of its services, support systemic improvements and sustain collaboration in bridging gaps between taxpayers and revenue authorities.

Mr. Olufemi Adewole, representing the Depot and Petroleum Products Marketers Association of Nigeria (DAPPMAN), highlighted the significant operational and fiscal challenges confronting oil and gas marketers, particularly delays in VAT refunds and high working-capital costs.

He acknowledged the government’s revenue-generation needs but stressed that taxation should not contribute to escalating the cost of living. He therefore advocated regular reviews of fiscal policies affecting petroleum marketers to assess their impact on downstream operations.

Prince Olusegun Oduntan, National Vice President, Association of Nigerian Licensed Customs Agents (ANLCA) highlighted concerns over personal taxes, local government levies for various amenities, and the method of taxing based on total turnover rather than actual profit margins.

He emphasized the association’s intention to submit a detailed position paper to the Office of the Tax Ombud, seeking redress and more equitable tax assessment practices tailored to the realities of their business model.

The Town Hall Meeting was attended by representatives of the Nigerian Association of Small and Medium Enterprises (NASME), National Union of Road Transport Workers (NURTW), Nigerian Association of Small Scale Industrialists (NASSI), Nigeria Network of NGOs (NNNGO), Nigeria Employers’ Consultative Association (NECA), Lagos Hotel Owners and Managers Association, Association of Nigerian Licensed Customs Agents, Petroleum and Natural Gas Senior Staff Association of Nigeria (PENGASSAN), and Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN) among others.

The post Airline operators, customs agents, others back Tax Ombud, seek fairer tax system appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: NADDC wins The Sun Parastatal of the Year award
description:
Osanipin dedicates honour to staff, stakeholders

By Moses Akaigwe
The National Automotive Design and Development Council (NADDC), Abuja, was on Friday, November 13, presented with The Sun Parastatal of the Year 2026 award. It was one of the major highlights of this year’s The Sun Awards ceremony he
content:
• Osanipin dedicates honour to staff, stakeholders

By Moses Akaigwe

The National Automotive Design and Development Council (NADDC), Abuja, was on Friday, November 13, presented with The Sun Parastatal of the Year 2026 award. It was one of the major highlights of this year’s The Sun Awards ceremony held at Eko Hotels and Suites, Victoria Island, Lagos.

The award marked a historic milestone in the history of The Sun Awards, as the Parastatal of the Year category was introduced for the first time at the ceremony, which was described at the venue as the Best (awards ceremony)  in Africa.

The Director-General of NADDC, Otunba Oluwemimo Joseph Osanipin, received the prestigious award on behalf of the Council. He was accompanied to the stage by his wife, the Chairman of the Council’s Governing Board, Chief Emma Eneukwu, and a Board member and National Coordinator of the Association of Local Content Manufacturers of Nigeria (ALCMAN), Chief Anselm Ilekuba.

Speaking with journalists after receiving the award, Osanipin described the recognition as pleasantly surprising, saying that neither he nor anyone in the Council had lobbied for or anticipated the honour.

He said it was particularly gratifying to discover that the editors of a reputable national newspaper like The Sun had been quietly monitoring the efforts of the NADDC’s management and staff over the past few years to reposition and uplift Nigeria’s automotive industry.

Describing the award as credible and highly rated, the Director-General said the recognition would further motivate the Council to intensify efforts towards fulfilling its mandate of developing and transforming the Nigerian automotive industry.

Osanipin also described the honour as an acknowledgement of the collective efforts being made to advance local automotive manufacturing, promote investment, strengthen indigenous capacity and drive the implementation of the Nigerian Automotive Industry Development Plan (NAIDP) 2023–2033.

He dedicated the award to the Council’s management and staff, while acknowledging the support of the Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment, automotive industry stakeholders, development partners and private-sector collaborators.

He reaffirmed NADDC’s commitment to strengthening Nigeria’s automotive value chain, attracting investments and positioning the country as a competitive destination for automotive manufacturing.

In the Nigerian automotive sector, the recognition is expected to provide further impetus to the Council’s ongoing initiatives in industrial development, technology transfer, skills acquisition, local content promotion and the transition towards cleaner automotive technologies.

Since Osanipin assumed office as Director-General in October 2023, NADDC has embarked on a series of initiatives and interventions aimed at strengthening the country’s automotive ecosystem and creating opportunities for local manufacturers, technicians and other industry participants.

Among the notable achievements is the expansion of Automotive Training and CNG Conversion Centres across the country. The Council has established and commissioned centres in Kano, Lagos, Potiskum in Yobe State, Zamfara and Kebbi states, providing facilities for technical training, CNG vehicle conversion, certification and skills acquisition.

The Council has also played a significant role in advancing Nigeria’s transition towards alternative automotive energy sources through the nationwide accreditation of CNG conversion workshops. More than 300 workshops have been accredited, helping to promote safety, quality assurance and standardisation in the growing CNG conversion industry.

In furtherance of its clean mobility agenda, NADDC introduced National Occupational Standards for the conversion, calibration and maintenance of autogas-powered vehicles, as well as electric vehicle servicing and maintenance.

It also partnered with the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) to equip young Nigerians with practical skills in CNG conversion and alternative fuel technologies.

Another significant intervention was the Council’s partnership with the Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation (CrediCorp), through which a N20 billion consumer credit fund was launched in December 2024 to facilitate the purchase of locally assembled vehicles. The initiative is designed to improve vehicle affordability, stimulate demand and support domestic automotive production.

On the regulatory front, NADDC, in collaboration with the Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON), introduced the Vehicle Conformity Assessment Programme (VehCAP) to improve vehicle safety, quality assurance and consumer protection. The Council also launched the End-of-Life Vehicle Recycling Regulation to promote environmentally sustainable vehicle disposal and resource recovery.

In April 2026, it further introduced the National Vehicle Dealership Registration Framework to modernise dealership operations, improve transparency and strengthen consumer protection in the Nigerian automotive market.

The Council has equally intensified efforts to develop indigenous automotive technology and encourage innovation among young Nigerians. These include the CNG Hybrid Vehicle Design Challenge and an eight-seater electric shuttle bus design competition involving universities across the country’s six geopolitical zones.

In the area of human capital development, NADDC trained more than 1,200 artisans and automotive technicians in 2025 in areas including mechatronics, CNG conversion, heavy-duty vehicle maintenance, modern automotive diagnostics and vehicle servicing.

A further boost to local manufacturing came in February 2026 with the launch of the Import Deletion Programme for Local Automotive Components and Parts. The initiative is aimed at reducing dependence on imported components, encouraging indigenous manufacturing, increasing local content utilisation and strengthening Nigeria’s automotive supply chain.

The Council has also strengthened its institutional collaboration and policy advocacy through strategic engagement with the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP), aimed at promoting the patronage of locally assembled vehicles and advancing the Federal Government’s Nigeria First Policy.

To deepen public awareness and industry engagement, NADDC launched Automotive Hour, described as Nigeria’s first dedicated automotive television talk show. The programme provides a platform for discussions on automotive policies, local manufacturing, investment opportunities, clean mobility and skills development.

These initiatives form part of the Council’s broader efforts to address longstanding challenges confronting Nigeria’s automotive industry, particularly low local production capacity utilisation, dependence on imported components, inadequate technical skills and limited market patronage for locally assembled vehicles.

The Sun Parastatal of the Year 2026 award, therefore, comes as a recognition of the Council’s contributions to automotive industry development and the implementation of programmes intended to strengthen the country’s domestic manufacturing capacity.

Apart from the NADDC Governing Board Chairman, Chief Eneukwu; and Member, Chief Anselm Ilekuba who is also the Chairman of Cedric Masters Group, others that accompanied  the DG to the stage included the Director of Human Resources Management (HRM), Mrs. Ronke Amodu; Director of Press and Public Relations, Mrs Susan Bisong-Taiwo;  and the Deputy Director of Press and Public Relations, Ike Okoha.

The post NADDC wins The Sun Parastatal of the Year award appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Without manufacturing $1tr economy is an illusion
description:
By Dele Sobowale







Japan in fact offers a relevant historical example of what can happen to an economy which falls behind in the global manufacturing race. Even in Africa, the Giant of Africa is lagging behind at least three other economies in the scale and scope of manufacturing. Consequently,
content:
By Dele Sobowale

Japan in fact offers a relevant historical example of what can happen to an economy which falls behind in the global manufacturing race. Even in Africa, the Giant of Africa is lagging behind at least three other economies in the scale and scope of manufacturing. Consequently, the politically-motivated promise to make Nigeria a one trillion dollar economy by 2030 is only one of the many illusions of the Tinubu administration. Desirable as it is, a $1 trillion economy is unachievable for reasons too numerous to discuss now, but, the cardinal reason is Nigeria’s weak manufacturing base – forcing us to import thousands of products which we can, with little effort, produce locally.

I was a Senior Lecturer/Consultant working with the Nigerian Institute of Management, NIM, in 1992, when Morita wrote the article in which that statement was made. The NIM Library was my second home and office. When not busy teaching courses in Sales, Marketing and General Management, I was in the Library reading and gathering materials for my lectures, as well as my book of quotations, VBQ – which was published in 2007. Japan was the world’s second largest manufacturing economy as well as the second largest economy; and was threatening the American leadership in that regard. Several books were written on the Art of Japanese Management; leading American Business Schools included courses in Japanese business methods in their curricula as compulsory subjects. The Japanese economy was growing at 7 to 10 per cent annually; and projections were made regarding when it would overtake the US as the largest economy globally. China and India were nowhere in sight. Then, something happened.

Science and technology brought new products which called for new and modern factories. Western investors, scared by Japan’s growing economic prowess, diverted investments to other Asian economies – South Korea, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and China. Gradually, several South East Asian nations started challenging Japan in sectors such as electronics and ship building. Unnoticeable at first, but the steady erosion of Japanese share of global manufacturing eventually took its toll. Today, the second and third leading manufacturers are China and India. China is now the largest manufacturer; hotly pursued by China. Japan has dropped to the fifth position in global ranking measured in terms of Gross Domestic Productivity, GDP. China, not Japan, is now threatening the US leadership. Manufacturing is the primary reason for that change in the fortunes of nations.

Nigeria Is Missing The Boat Once Again

“Those who do not remember the past are condemned to repeat it.”

George Santayana, 1863-1952, VBQ p 93.

It might be difficult for the Generation Z youths to believe that Nigeria once embarked on rapid industrialization. The Gowon administration sent delegations to the United States in 1974 to appeal to young and well-educated Nigerians to return home and fill vacant positions opening up in manufacturing in several industrial layouts in Lagos, Ibadan, Kaduna, Kano, Portharcourt and Aba. I was one of those who responded to the call to return home and help Nigeria’s transformation to a manufacturing giant. On arrival in August 1974, my first working experience was at the Ilupeju Industrial Layout in Lagos. I soon discovered there were others in Lagos State – Ikeja, Iganmu and Apapa. My first trip to Portharcourt and Aba revealed the Trans Amadi and Ogbor Hill layouts respectively; the Northern legs of the national familiarization tour took me to Kano’s Bompai, Kaduna and Anglo Jos in Plateau state. Granted, everything I saw could not have been more than a few establishments on Route 128, Massachusetts, USA – where I gained industrial experience. But it was a promising start. Construction of new factories and expansion of old factories was going on at feverish pace. Jobs were available everywhere. I left manufacturing enterprises in 1990 after working in five different industrial layouts. The last was in Kalambina, Sokoto State.

Unfortunately, the 16 years between 1974 and 1990 represented the period of the rise and decline of manufacturing in Nigeria. Instead of building on what we started, gradual decline set in. SPARS, a retail outlet, has replaced our factory for analgesics and cough syrup. The brewery in Bompai lies in ruins; and the rice mill in Sokoto remains shut since 1991. Right now, the current reforms embarked upon by President Tinubu threaten to again set in motion the process which made manufacturing extremely difficult in Nigeria.

Current Situation: No Power; Expensive Credit

“Power supply plunges as gas shortage, water level worsen.”

VANGUARD, November 6, 2026

Manufacturing became very attractive in the 1970s when the Kainji Hydro Power Station was established. None of the industrial estates could have been started without relatively reliable public power supply. Definitely, Nigerian Paper Mill, Jeba; Nigerian Sugar Company, NISUCO and the Nigerian Yeast and Alcohol Manufacturing Company, both at Bacita, Kwara State could not have been started if they had to operate on generators. I was a consultant for the three; and I recall the discussions with their Chief Executive Officers. Without exception, they were certain their companies could not survive on generators. They were absolutely correct. On November 5, 2026, Nigeria was able to supply only 2,926MW to the entire nation. That is deeply concerning for two reasons. One, we achieved capacity to generate 4,000MW per day as far back as 2012. Fourteen years later, the Federal Government is still offering the same excuses for remaining stuck at 4,000MW on a good day. No $1 trillion economy generates less than 45,000MW. South Africa is Africa’s largest economy, far less than the $1 trillion economy. But, it already provides more than 45,000MW.

“Banks’ loan to manufacturers slumps 26.8% to N5.19trn.”

VANGUARD, October 26, 2026.

Credit is the soul of business and has been an axiom for several hundred years. Banks and financial institutions were established primarily to promote businesses; not to finance government deficits. The Great Depression in the last century, as well as the rise of Keynesianism, gave rise to governments invading banks to borrow funds for their operations. Deficit spending, once proposed as a short-term measure, has hardened into a permanent feature of fiscal policy. Very few governments now attempt to balance their budgets. Reliance on deficit spending and perpetual borrowing is the new normal. In the process, banks are increasingly called upon to extend credits to the government. Private sector borrowers, especially manufacturers are bearing the brunt of the new situation.

Nigerian manufacturers are being hammered three ways. First, they don’t receive as much as they would want. Second, the interest rates are exorbitant. Third, they compete against foreign producers whose governments provide support across the board and whose banks charge single digit interest rates. How we expect Nigerian manufacturers paying 30 per cent to compete with Chinese paying 2 per cent remains a mystery to me.

Follow me on Facebook @ J Israel Biola

The post Without manufacturing $1tr economy is an illusion appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 16, 2026
description:
The Nigerian naira opened Monday, November 16, 2026, under mild pressure across the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) while maintaining relative stability in the parallel market.



At the official window, data published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) shows the NFEM rate referen
content:
The Nigerian naira opened Monday, November 16, 2026, under mild pressure across the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) while maintaining relative stability in the parallel market.

At the official window, data published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) shows the NFEM rate referencing ₦1,353.97 per dollar. This follows a ₦7.18 depreciation in the preceding session as corporate foreign exchange obligations and seasonal end-of-year import demand weighed on liquidity. Meanwhile, spot interbank indicators in early morning trading hovered around ₦1,343.35 per dollar as dealers awaited fresh intraday price discovery.

In the parallel market, also known as the black market, Bureau De Change (BDC) operators and street dealers in Lagos and Abuja quoted the US dollar at a buying rate of ₦1,380 and a selling rate of ₦1,390.

With the official rate standing at ₦1,353.97 and the parallel market selling at ₦1,390, the exchange rate spread between both markets sits at approximately ₦36.03 per dollar. Market analysts note that steady foreign reserve buffers and ongoing CBN market interventions continue to keep the disparity between the official and unofficial segments within a narrow band compared to historical volatility.

title: 1,960 Flights Cancelled On Sunday Alone, As US Airport Disruption Enters Day Three
description: An additional 1,960 flights were cancelled on Sunday alone as the widespread disruption following an extraordinary no-takeoff order issued by US aviation authorities entered its third day on Monday.About 6,000 flights were cancelled at the weekend, leaving thousands of passengers stranded at airport
content:
An additional 1,960 flights were cancelled on Sunday alone as the widespread disruption following an extraordinary no-takeoff order issued by US aviation authorities entered its third day on Monday.

About 6,000 flights were cancelled at the weekend, leaving thousands of passengers stranded at airports.

The ground stop issued Friday afternoon was only the second time such a directive had been issued nationwide in the busy US airspace since planes were grounded following the 9/11 attacks. It was blamed by the Trump administration on a faulty upgrade to communications equipment.

As of Sunday evening, more than 55 US-related flights — those traveling within, into or out of the United States — scheduled for Monday were cancelled, according to industry tracker FlightAware.

That marked a dramatic shift from the more than 1,960 flights cancelled on Sunday.

The Trump administration sought to reassure weary flyers as questions remained over how such chaos could unfold in the world’s largest economy, a country that prides itself on its technological prowess.

Throughout the weekend, stranded passengers wandered through chaotic airports and sat on floors, waiting for updates or to be rebooked.

Officials blamed Friday’s colossal snafu on faulty work to upgrade air traffic control communication cables.

President Donald Trump on Sunday ended uncharacteristic days of silence on the ground stop, but only to blame his predecessor Joe Biden for the debacle.

Trump insisted he inherited a mess from the Biden administration and said Congress, which his party has controlled for two years, must approve funds to upgrade America’s outdated air traffic control system.

“The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster,” Trump said, referring to the Federal Aviation Administration.

“Everything they touched turned bad. Big money spent unwisely, making an old and broken system worse than when they began,” Trump asserted.

FAA chief Bryan Bedford had said Saturday that air travel for millions of Americans stranded at airports would return to normal by the close of business on Sunday.

But Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Sunday morning it will actually take longer to get planes, crews and travelers to where they need to be.

“So, in the airspace, we’re going to see things come back to normal today, but probably fully normal tomorrow,” Duffy said on ABC News.

“We had airplanes and crews out of position because of Friday, so it takes a little bit of time to do that.”

‘I’m The Secretary’

Duffy also flatly rejected calls for his resignation over the travel chaos, insisting he inherited woefully outdated air traffic control infrastructure, such as, he said, radar equipment that dates back to the 1960s.

“So when we do work and things go wrong, of course I’m the secretary. But I also have to acknowledge what was delivered to me,” Duffy said in an interview on CNN.

The ground stop not only plunged US air travel into chaos, it also raised serious concerns about the country’s aging infrastructure.

Duffy has appealed for $50 billion in funds to upgrade and modernize the air traffic control system, and called for Congress, which controls the purse strings of the US government, to “meet this moment.”

But Democrats quickly pounced to say Congress under Trump’s Republicans could already have done this.

AFP

title: Canada bars Russian team entry into 2026 Junior Ice Hockey World championships
description:
Russia’s bid to return to international sports has suffered another setback after Canada announced plans to prevent Russian athletes from entering the country for the 2026 Junior Ice Hockey World Championships.
The decision effectively rules out Russia’s Under-20 national team from participating in
content:
Russia’s bid to return to international sports has suffered another setback after Canada announced plans to prevent Russian athletes from entering the country for the 2026 Junior Ice Hockey World Championships.

The decision effectively rules out Russia’s Under-20 national team from participating in the tournament, scheduled to take place from December 26, 2026, to January 5, 2027, in Edmonton and Red Deer.

According to BBC Sport on Monday, the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) confirmed Russia’s exclusion in a statement, citing restrictions communicated by the Canadian government.

“Due to the position and restrictions formally communicated by the Canadian government, the Russian Under-20 national team is unable to participate in the World Junior Championship,” the IIHF said.

The federation added that, after considering alternative arrangements, it had decided to retain Canada as the host nation.

“After carefully assessing the feasibility of alternative arrangements, the IIHF Council has determined that Canada will remain as host and the tournament will proceed from 26 December 2026 to 5 January 2027 in Edmonton and Red Deer,” it said.

Russia’s exclusion has drawn criticism from the Russian Ice Hockey Federation, which described the decision as “unacceptable and unlawful” and vowed to appeal to the International Olympic Committee (IOC).

“The IIHF’s decision was made solely due to political reasons.

“The exclusion of the Russian national team violates fundamental legal principles, Olympism, the principle of non-discrimination, equality among athletes and the integrity of international tournaments,” the Russian federation said in a statement.

Russia had been suspended from IIHF competitions since its invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

However, the Court of Arbitration for Sport overturned the ban last month, ruling that the federation’s safety and security arguments were “not supported by sufficient evidence”.

The court subsequently ordered the IIHF to allow Russia to participate in its competitions.

The ruling was welcomed by Russia but opposed by Ukraine and some sponsors of the Junior World Championships.
The situation became more complicated after six European ice hockey federations threatened to boycott matches against Russia if the country were allowed to participate.

Canada’s decision to deny entry to Russian athletes has now effectively ended hopes of Russia featuring in the tournament.

The development is part of a wider debate over Russia’s possible return to international sport following its invasion of Ukraine.

Norway, Finland and Estonia have also announced plans to block visas for Russian and Belarusian athletes.

Norway is preparing to host the Cross-Country World Cup next month, while Finland is scheduled to stage the World Figure Skating Championships in March.

The International Skating Union (ISU), however, has defended the participation rights of athletes, saying it believes they should not be penalised for the actions of their governments.

“The ISU believes that athletes should not be punished for the actions of their governments in a world where, sadly, many conflicts are ongoing,” the organisation said, adding that it was “seeking clarifications” from Finnish officials.

Meanwhile, several Russian and Belarusian athletes were allowed to compete under their national flags at the Winter Paralympics in March after the International Paralympic Committee lifted some restrictions.

In July, the IOC also provisionally reinstated Russia to its competitions, declaring that a ban introduced in 2023 was “no longer applicable”.

However, individual international sports federations retain the authority to determine their own eligibility requirements.

While World Gymnastics, World Aquatics and World Boxing have lifted restrictions on Russian athletes, World Athletics has maintained its ban.

Last month, Moscow was announced as the host of the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships, marking the first time an Olympic sports federation has awarded Russia a global event since the country invaded Ukraine.

title: ICYMI: Tinubu approves recruitment of 28,000 soldiers, 50,000 police officers
description:
President Bola Tinubu has approved the recruitment of 28,000 additional soldiers and 50,000 police officers as part of efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s security architecture and tackle insecurity across the country.
The approval forms part of the administration’s proposed Five-Year Strategic Defence
content:
President Bola Tinubu has approved the recruitment of 28,000 additional soldiers and 50,000 police officers as part of efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s security architecture and tackle insecurity across the country.

The approval forms part of the administration’s proposed Five-Year Strategic Defence Operations Plan, designed to improve military effectiveness, expand operational capacity and strengthen the country’s response to terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other criminal activities.

The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council disclosed this in a press statement issued on Sunday by its spokesperson, Dele Alake.

According to the statement, the President’s decision to increase military manpower is aimed at strengthening the presence of troops on the ground and enhancing operational effectiveness.

“To further the manpower expansion drive, President Tinubu also approved recruiting an additional 28,000 soldiers to strengthen the military’s presence on the ground and enhance its operational effectiveness,” the statement said.

It added that the President had also approved the recruitment of 50,000 additional police officers “as part of broader efforts to reinforce internal security, improve policing capacity, and strengthen the country’s response to criminal activities.”

The campaign council further disclosed that Tinubu had created four new Army divisions and restructured existing military formations to expand operational coverage and improve responses to security threats.

It said the administration had also approved the establishment of two additional Army depots in Osogbo, Osun State, and Amasiri-Edda, Ebonyi State, to increase military training capacity and accelerate the recruitment of soldiers.

“Each depot can accommodate 6,000 recruits at a time, bringing their combined training capacity to 12,000 soldiers,” the statement noted.

It added that 5,210 recruits were already undergoing training at the Osogbo facility.

The statement also highlighted the administration’s investment in military accommodation and operational infrastructure, including a 700-unit military barracks project in Ikere-Ekiti, Ekiti State.

On the fight against insurgency, the APC Presidential Campaign Council claimed that military operations across the country had resulted in the elimination of more than 15,000 Boko Haram terrorists and bandits in the last three years.

It also claimed that over 130,000 Boko Haram fighters and their dependents had surrendered through Operation Safe Corridor, the Federal Government’s rehabilitation programme for repentant insurgents.

The council said the proposed Five-Year Strategic Defence Operations Plan would provide a long-term framework for aligning defence priorities, operational requirements, capability development and expenditure with Nigeria’s security challenges.

“The initiative is a major component of President Tinubu’s determination to reposition the nation’s security architecture toward a more coordinated, intelligence-led, technology-enabled, and prevention-oriented system capable of addressing terrorism, banditry, kidnapping, and other forms of criminality,” the statement said.

The council maintained that the combination of sustained military operations, improved manpower, modern technology and non-kinetic interventions would strengthen the country’s capacity to address insecurity.

title: Stock market rebounds as investors reap N2.2trn amid decline in oil price
description:
By Peter Egwuatu 







The Nigerian stock market rebounded last week after weeks of sustained pressure from profit taking led to decline in stock value.







Equity investors on the Nigerian Exchange Limited, NGX, last week, reaped over N2.2 trillion in capital gains leading the NGX market capit
content:
By Peter Egwuatu

The Nigerian stock market rebounded last week after weeks of sustained pressure from profit taking led to decline in stock value.

Equity investors on the Nigerian Exchange Limited, NGX, last week, reaped over N2.2 trillion in capital gains leading the NGX market capitalisation, to close last week at N163.795 trillion, up from N161.593 trillion the previous week.

Similarly, another major market performance indicator, NGX All Share Index, ASI, surged by 1.4 % to close at 252,269.16 points from 248,877.22 points the previous week, indicating renewed demand for selected heavyweight stocks, which dominated the market.

Analysts noted that although buying interests remained evident in major banking and industrial stocks , the broader market reflected a mixed trading pattern, with investors maintaining selective positions amid intermittent profit-taking in several stocks

The positive performance, according to analysts, highlights the continued resilience of the domestic stock market, which has maintained substantial gains since the beginning of the year.

Reacting to market performance and outlook analysts at InvestData Consulting Limited, said : “ The immediate market outlook remains cautiously positive, supported by the strong year-to-date return and continued interest in selected large-cap stocks. Nevertheless, investors are likely to maintain a selective approach, considering corporate earnings, dividend expectations, valuation levels and prevailing macroeconomic conditions before increasing their exposure. The possibility of further profit-taking cannot be ruled out, particularly in stocks that have recorded significant gains in recent sessions.

Overall, the market appears to be consolidating its recent advances while maintaining an underlying bullish bias. The ability of the index to break above the 255,000-point resistance level, alongside improved market participation, will be important in determining whether the current upward movement can extend into another phase of appreciation.” They further noted that the political outcome of the US midterm elections introduced additional uncertainty into the market adding that the developments have placed renewed attention on the possibility of diplomatic negotiations and their implications for global crude supply.

“For Nigeria, the movement in international crude prices remains particularly important given the country’s dependence on oil exports for foreign exchange earnings and government revenue. A sustained decline in crude prices could place additional pressure on projected oil receipts, especially if production levels remain below expectations. Conversely, elevated prices could support external earnings, although the benefits would depend on domestic production performance, export volumes and fiscal management” the analysts added.

title: Hundreds of Nigerian travellers stranded as US flight cancellation persists
description:
Hundreds of Nigerian travellers have been affected by widespread flight cancellations in the United States following a nationwide air traffic control ground stop that began on Friday.
The disruption, which affected thousands of flights across the US, has also disrupted international aviation operati
content:
Hundreds of Nigerian travellers have been affected by widespread flight cancellations in the United States following a nationwide air traffic control ground stop that began on Friday.

The disruption, which affected thousands of flights across the US, has also disrupted international aviation operations, leaving passengers travelling from Nigeria to the United States and those scheduled to return home facing delays, cancellations and uncertainty.

Findings by Very Nigerian showed that several Nigerian passengers scheduled to travel to the US over the weekend could not embark on their journeys as planned.

Some of the affected travellers were forced to temporarily abandon their trips, while others postponed their flights pending the restoration of normal airline operations.

Some perssengers temporarily spent hours within the airport terminal while some others checked into a hotel around the airport with the thought that the disruptions would only last for a day.

A passenger, Sola Aina, who spoke with our correspondent on Sunday, said he had been forced to return home after spending days waiting for his flight to be rescheduled.

“I just have to return home today. I have come for a Friday flight before we heard of the troubles in the U.S, I have to sleep in a hotel since Friday believing that the issues would be sorted before Sunday night, but this is almost 7:00pm again now.

“I have ordered a cab. I have to return to Ibadan. It’s very painful but I don’t have an option,” he said.

Another passenger, Faruq Akinwale, said the disruption had affected his plans to return home urgently, as his wife and sick child were in the US.

“I have a sick child with my wife in the U.S and I need to return home urgently, but what do I do? But I understand that no one can be blamed for this, but I will only appeal that everyone concerned should please hasten up whatever they are doing, I pray God help them,” he said.

A mother of two, Mrs Aderemi, also expressed disappointment over the situation, saying she and her family had been left with little choice but to return home.

“We will just return home, the situation is just understandable even though it’s painful,” she said.

Similarly, another passenger, Charles Adekunle, said the disruption had affected his travel plans, although he did not disclose whether he intended to reschedule his trip.

The situation has also affected passengers travelling from the US to Nigeria, particularly those booked on international services connecting major American cities to Lagos and Abuja.

Airlines operating flights between Nigeria and the US, either directly or through connecting routes, include Qatar Airways, Turkish Airlines, Ethiopian Airlines, Emirates, Virgin Atlantic and British Airways, among others.

Although the Federal Aviation Administration lifted the nationwide ground stop on Saturday evening, airlines have continued to battle operational challenges, including the repositioning of aircraft and flight crews displaced by the disruption.

An update published on Delta Air Lines’ website on Saturday indicated that the carrier was still working to restore normal operations following the FAA-mandated ground stop, which lasted more than four hours.

The airline said passengers scheduled to travel between 13 and 15 November, 2026, could change their bookings without paying additional charges.

It also encouraged customers with flexible travel arrangements to move their flights to Monday, 16 November, or later, warning that passengers travelling over the weekend should expect delays and further schedule adjustments.

Delta said, “Delta continues to restore operations following an FAA-mandated nationwide ground stop that lasted more than four hours on Friday, November 13. Customers traveling today should expect delays and additional schedule adjustments as we work to reposition flight crews and aircraft.

“Taking care of customers remains our focus, and we continue to offer flexible rebooking options to change flights at no extra cost. Customers who have flexible travel plans are encouraged to move their flights to Monday, Nov. 16 or later.

“If you are traveling on Saturday, please allow extra time and check the Delta app or delta.com for the latest flight status and travel information. Delta will provide customers with as much notice as possible about changes to flight schedules. When a cancellation does occur, Delta will automatically rebook customers to the next best itinerary.”

Meanwhile, the Donald Trump administration has warned that disruptions to air travel across the United States could persist until Monday, extending the wait for a full return to normal operations.

Hundreds more flights were cancelled on Sunday, raising concerns about the scale of the disruption in the world’s largest economy, which has one of the busiest aviation networks globally.

US officials attributed Friday’s disruption to faulty work carried out during an upgrade of air traffic control communication cables.

President Donald Trump broke his silence on the crisis on Sunday, blaming the previous administration of Joe Biden for the state of the country’s air traffic control infrastructure.

The FAA chief, Bryan Bedford, had said on Saturday that air travel for millions of Americans affected by the disruption would return to normal by the close of business on Sunday.

However, Transportation Secretary, Sean Duffy, said on Sunday that the restoration of normal operations would take longer because aircraft and flight crews had been displaced during the disruption.

The post Hundreds of Nigerian travellers stranded as US flight cancellation persists appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Mayweather visits Sanwo-Olu in Lagos, set to launch boxing academy (Photos)
description:
American boxing legend Floyd Mayweather Jr. on Sunday paid a courtesy visit to Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, at Lagos House, Marina, during his visit to Nigeria.
The undefeated former five-division world champion is in the country to introduce the TMT Frontrow Fight Series, a grassroots
content:
American boxing legend Floyd Mayweather Jr. on Sunday paid a courtesy visit to Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, at Lagos House, Marina, during his visit to Nigeria.

The undefeated former five-division world champion is in the country to introduce the TMT Frontrow Fight Series, a grassroots boxing initiative aimed at discovering and developing young Nigerian talents.

The programme is expected to provide opportunities for aspiring boxers through training academies and development schemes planned for Lagos, Abuja, Enugu, Calabar and other cities across the country.

The initiative is designed to identify, train and promote emerging Nigerian boxers, providing them with platforms to develop their skills and pursue professional boxing careers.

The first event is scheduled for 2027, with Mayweather also expected to take part in a boxing contest in Nigeria that year.

Sanwo-Olu welcomed the boxing icon and expressed the state’s readiness to partner on the project.

In a post obtained from Sanwo-Olu’s X handle on Monday, the governor was quoted as saying, “It was a pleasure to receive American professional boxing champion Floyd Mayweather Jr. at Lagos House, Marina.

“His vision of inspiring grassroots boxing talent across Africa, starting here in Nigeria, and bringing international boxing events to Lagos presents opportunities for our young people and the sports industry.

“Lagos is ready to welcome major sporting events. We have continued to invest in sports infrastructure and we are focused on creating an environment where talent can grow and succeed.

“We look forward to exploring these opportunities and strengthening Lagos’s place as a leading destination for sports and entertainment in Africa.”

Earlier, Mayweather also met the Director-General of the Lagos State Sports Commission, Lekan Fatodu, who described Lagos as an ideal location for boxing events and praised the state’s sports infrastructure under Sanwo-Olu’s administration.

Mayweather’s visit comes ahead of his scheduled exhibition bout against Australian boxer Matt “The Jedi” Floyd in Bangkok, Thailand, on December 19, 2026.

The engagement has generated excitement among Nigerian boxing fans, who see the involvement of one of the sport’s biggest global stars as a boost for grassroots talent and the potential to host more international boxing events in Lagos.

Very Nigerian reported that Mayweather was set to launch a boxing development initiative in Nigeria to discover, train, and promote emerging talent.

Frank, who is the Ambassador to East Africa and the Middle East of the United Liberation Movement for West Papua, ULMWP, said Nigerians would not accept an outcome that contradicts their votes.

“Nigerians will not accept a situation in which someone is declared the winner when the people know they did not vote for him. They should not push the country into a crisis by attempting to impose him on the people,” he warned.

Urging the president to abandon his re-election ambition and guarantee a transparent electoral process, he said: “Whoever wins should be allowed to emerge as the choice of the people.”

Frank also expressed concern over alleged attempts by some political actors to manipulate the electoral process.

He described the public protest against Tinubu after prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in Area 1, Garki, Abuja, last Friday as evidence of growing dissatisfaction with the administration.

Tinubu reportedly faced boos from some Hausa protesters who chanted “Ba ma yi” (we don’t want you) after the prayers. In a viral video, some protesters were seen removing and destroying his campaign posters and billboards in parts of Area 1.

Frank condemned the protesters for choosing a religious occasion to vent their displeasure and commended the President’s security detail for ensuring his safety and de-escalating the situation.

He nevertheless urged the President to recognise the significance of the public reaction.

“The rejection was total and unmistakable. No Nigerian president has been embarrassed like this publicly. The way Nigerians rejected him speaks volumes but should he decide to go ahead and he loses, he should be prepared to accept defeat just like former President Goodluck Jonathan did,” he said.

The former APC spokesman said he was worried by what he called a growing gap between the assurances given to the President by political associates and the mood of the people.

“I have seen the confidence with which some people are assuring President Tinubu that he will win the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, and that he is firmly in control. But the reported embarrassment he suffered during a prayer session in Abuja tells a different story.

“What happened in the FCT last Friday showed that political assurances and promises are not necessarily a reflection of the reality on the ground. The public reaction reflects the anger and dissatisfaction of Nigerians, which those around the President may not be telling him about.

“What happened in FCT and Jos after the APC rally has shown that people like the FCT minister, Nyesom Wike promising him 80 percent of votes in Abuja and the Governor of Edo State, Monday Okpebholo vowing to give him 2.5 million votes in Edo State, would disappoint him due to the reality on ground.

“Those telling him to continue and assuring him that he will win the next election are merely deceiving him. Even some people within his political circle, including those involved in his campaign, know that selling his candidacy to Nigerians will be difficult,” Frank said.

He alleged that financial considerations were influencing the positions of some political associates, and said the President needed honest assessments of his performance and popularity.

“I am giving him this advice because I genuinely want him to listen to the truth. Those around him may not be telling him that he has become very unpopular and that continuing in the presidential race may be a difficult undertaking. My advice is that he should take a bow and leave the race. He should take this advice seriously,” he said.

Frank urged Tinubu to take a cue from opposition figures, including former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State governor, Peter Obi, whom he said draw large crowds without financial inducements.

“Wherever these opposition leaders go, Nigerians come out in large numbers to receive them without being induced with rice or money. Their reception should tell the President something about the mood of the country,” he said.

He listed hunger, unemployment, rising living costs and insecurity among the factors fuelling public anger.

“If the President had performed well, there would be no need for the desperation we are witnessing today,” he said.

Frank also questioned the credibility of endorsements for the President, alleging that some individuals and groups were motivated by anticipated financial benefits rather than genuine public sentiment.

“President Tinubu still has an opportunity to make history and have his name written in gold. He can achieve this by ensuring that the country conducts a free, fair and credible election,” he said.

title: Canada denies Russian team entry for ice hockey tournament
description:
Russia’s hopes of returning to international sport have suffered another setback after Canada announced plans to deny Russian athletes entry to the 2026 Junior Ice Hockey World Championships.
The Canadian government’s decision effectively bars Russia’s Under-20 national team from participating in th
content:
Russia’s hopes of returning to international sport have suffered another setback after Canada announced plans to deny Russian athletes entry to the 2026 Junior Ice Hockey World Championships.

The Canadian government’s decision effectively bars Russia’s Under-20 national team from participating in the tournament, which is scheduled to hold from December 26, 2026, to January 5, 2027, in Edmonton and Red Deer.

As reported by BBC Sport on Monday, the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) confirmed Russia’s exclusion in a statement, citing restrictions communicated by the Canadian government.

“Due to the position and restrictions formally communicated by the Canadian government, the Russian Under-20 national team is unable to participate in the World Junior Championship,” the IIHF said.

The federation added that, after considering alternative arrangements, it had decided to retain Canada as the host nation.

“After carefully assessing the feasibility of alternative arrangements, the IIHF Council has determined that Canada will remain as host and the tournament will proceed from 26 December 2026 to 5 January 2027 in Edmonton and Red Deer,” it said.

Russia’s exclusion has drawn criticism from the Russian Ice Hockey Federation, which described the decision as “unacceptable and unlawful” and vowed to appeal to the International Olympic Committee (IOC).

“The IIHF’s decision was made solely due to political reasons.

“The exclusion of the Russian national team violates fundamental legal principles, Olympism, the principle of non-discrimination, equality among athletes and the integrity of international tournaments,” the Russian federation said in a statement.

Russia had been suspended from IIHF competitions since its invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

However, the Court of Arbitration for Sport overturned the ban last month, ruling that the federation’s safety and security arguments were “not supported by sufficient evidence”.

The court subsequently ordered the IIHF to allow Russia to participate in its competitions.

The ruling was welcomed by Russia but opposed by Ukraine and some sponsors of the Junior World Championships.

The situation became more complicated after six European ice hockey federations threatened to boycott matches against Russia if the country were allowed to participate.

Canada’s decision to deny entry to Russian athletes has now effectively ended hopes of Russia featuring in the tournament.

The development is part of a wider debate over Russia’s possible return to international sport following its invasion of Ukraine.

Norway, Finland and Estonia have also announced plans to block visas for Russian and Belarusian athletes.

Norway is preparing to host the Cross-Country World Cup next month, while Finland is scheduled to stage the World Figure Skating Championships in March.

The International Skating Union (ISU), however, has defended the participation rights of athletes, saying it believes they should not be penalised for the actions of their governments.

“The ISU believes that athletes should not be punished for the actions of their governments in a world where, sadly, many conflicts are ongoing,” the organisation said, adding that it was “seeking clarifications” from Finnish officials.

Meanwhile, several Russian and Belarusian athletes were allowed to compete under their national flags at the Winter Paralympics in March after the International Paralympic Committee lifted some restrictions.

In July, the IOC also provisionally reinstated Russia to its competitions, declaring that a ban introduced in 2023 was “no longer applicable”.

However, individual international sports federations retain the authority to determine their own eligibility requirements.

While World Gymnastics, World Aquatics and World Boxing have lifted restrictions on Russian athletes, World Athletics has maintained its ban.

Last month, Moscow was announced as the host of the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships, marking the first time an Olympic sports federation has awarded Russia a global event since the country invaded Ukraine.

title: Fani-Kayode refused interview after live-stream ‘exclusion’ — SABC
description:
The South African Broadcasting Corporation, SABC, has said Nigeria’s High Commissioner to the country, Femi Fani-Kayode, declined an interview invitation, following his protest over the exclusion of his speech from a livestream of a diplomatic ceremony hosted by President Cyril Ramaphosa.



Read Al
content:
The South African Broadcasting Corporation, SABC, has said Nigeria’s High Commissioner to the country, Femi Fani-Kayode, declined an interview invitation, following his protest over the exclusion of his speech from a livestream of a diplomatic ceremony hosted by President Cyril Ramaphosa.

Read Also: South Africa releases Fani-Kayode’s speech after protest

The SABC, in a statement issued yesterday, said it regretted the envoy’s decision but remained open to engaging with him and the Nigerian High Commission.

The response followed Fani-Kayode’s complaint that his introduction and speech were omitted from the broadcaster’s livestream of the presentation of letters of credence ceremony held at the Sefako Makgatho Presidential Guest House in Pretoria on Friday.

“We regret that the High Commissioner declined an interview with SABC News, reportedly because of his dissatisfaction with the livestream of the ceremony. We respect his decision and remain open to engaging with him and the Nigerian High Commission,” the statement said.

Notably, the SABC did not address the specific allegation that Fani-Kayode’s presentation was excluded from the livestream of the ceremony.

It, however, rejected the description of it as a state broadcaster, insisting that it was a public service media organisation committed to independent, impartial and credible journalism.

“Two points need clarifying. First, the SABC is a public service media, not a state broadcaster. Our mandate is to serve the public interest through independent, impartial and credible journalism. The Presidency’s livestream arrangements and SABC News’ editorial coverage are separate matters.

“Secondly, SABC News did cover the ceremony. It was carried on the SABC News LIVE channel on SABC+, and the High Commissioner’s arrival was shown during a live crossing on the SABC News Channel (DStv Channel 404). We also published a clip on our official X account of the High Commissioner speaking to President Cyril Ramaphosa.

“The SABC remains committed to upholding the principles of fairness, impartiality and editorial independence in its coverage, as well as value our longstanding relationship with Nigeria,” the statement read.

Recall that Fani-Kayode had earlier accused the South African Presidency of deliberately excluding Nigeria’s delegation from the livestream of the ceremony, which involved 15 ambassadors presenting their letters of credence to Ramaphosa.

The envoy said the introductions and speeches of 14 other ambassadors were broadcast, while Nigeria’s segment was omitted, with the livestream resuming after he had concluded his address.

He also disclosed that he declined an interview offered by SABC News at the venue, saying he had been displeased with the treatment of the Nigerian delegation.

However, the South African Presidency later released the full video of the ceremony, including Fani-Kayode’s speech, on its YouTube channel.

The controversy subsequently sparked a public exchange between the Nigerian High Commission and Vincent Magwenya, spokesperson for Ramaphosa.

title: PHOTOS: Mayweather meets Sanwo-Olu, plans boxing academies in Nigeria
description:
American boxing legend Floyd Mayweather Jr. paid a courtesy visit to Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu at Lagos House, Marina, on Sunday as part of his trip to Nigeria to launch a major grassroots boxing initiative.
Mayweather, the undefeated former five-division world champion, is in the coun
content:
American boxing legend Floyd Mayweather Jr. paid a courtesy visit to Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu at Lagos House, Marina, on Sunday as part of his trip to Nigeria to launch a major grassroots boxing initiative.

Mayweather, the undefeated former five-division world champion, is in the country to introduce the TMT Frontrow Fight Series.

The programme aims to discover, train and promote young Nigerian boxers through academies and development schemes planned for Lagos, Abuja, Enugu, Calabar and other cities.

The first event is scheduled for 2027, with Mayweather also expected to take part in a boxing contest in Nigeria that year.

Sanwo-Olu welcomed the boxing icon and expressed the state’s readiness to partner on the project.

In a post obtained from Sanwo-Olu’s X handle on Monday, the governor was quoted as saying, “It was a pleasure to receive American professional boxing champion Floyd Mayweather Jr. at Lagos House, Marina.

“His vision of inspiring grassroots boxing talent across Africa, starting here in Nigeria, and bringing international boxing events to Lagos presents opportunities for our young people and the sports industry.

“Lagos is ready to welcome major sporting events. We have continued to invest in sports infrastructure and we are focused on creating an environment where talent can grow and succeed.

“We look forward to exploring these opportunities and strengthening Lagos’s place as a leading destination for sports and entertainment in Africa.”

Earlier, Mayweather also met the Director-General of the Lagos State Sports Commission, Lekan Fatodu, who described Lagos as an ideal location for boxing events and praised the state’s sports infrastructure under Sanwo-Olu’s administration.

Mayweather’s visit comes ahead of his scheduled exhibition bout against Australian boxer Matt “The Jedi” Floyd in Bangkok, Thailand, on December 19, 2026.

The engagement has generated excitement among Nigerian boxing fans, who see the involvement of one of the sport’s biggest global stars as a boost for grassroots talent and the potential to host more international boxing events in Lagos.

PUNCH Online reported that Mayweather was set to launch a boxing development initiative in Nigeria to discover, train, and promote emerging talent.

title: Economy Palava: Traders decry rising waybill ‘store keep’ charges
description:
By Elizabeth Adegbesan



Small-scale traders operating across major markets in the country have raised the alarm over arbitrary and escalating storage fees, locally known as “store keep money”, charged by transport operators and motor park agents on delayed waybills, warning that the practice is er
content:
By Elizabeth Adegbesan

Small-scale traders operating across major markets in the country have raised the alarm over arbitrary and escalating storage fees, locally known as “store keep money”, charged by transport operators and motor park agents on delayed waybills, warning that the practice is eroding their capital and threatening their livelihoods.

For many market women who rely on interstate commercial buses and trucks to restock goods such as foodstuffs, textiles, and household provisions, waybill logistics are the lifeline of daily commerce.

However, traders said the shrinking grace periods before daily demurrage charges kick in have turned routine restocking into a financial burden.

Economy&Lifestyle visits to some markets revealed a widespread frustration among traders, many of whom operate on thin profit margins and depend on daily turnover or microfinance loans to sustain their stalls.

Mrs. Grace Okafor, a wholesale dealer in dried seafood and condiments, recounted how a 24-hour delay caused by heavy rainfall cost her nearly half of her expected profit on a recent consignment.

“My goods arrived at the park late in the evening when no one could go out.

“By the time I got there the next afternoon with a tricycle to carry my sacks, the park officials insisted I had exceeded their grace period and demanded N6,000 for ‘store keep’.

“We cannot increase our selling prices because customers are already struggling to buy. That money came straight out of my capital.”

Other traders noted that the lack of standardized billing across motor parks leaves them vulnerable to exploitation, particularly when unforeseen emergencies delay pickup.

Mrs. Comfort Momoh, who trades in fabrics and wrappers, stated that arbitrary fee hikes are discouraging traders from ordering goods in bulk.

“There is no fixed rate or clear receipt for this store keep money; it depends on the mood of whoever is on duty at the park store,” she said.

“Sometimes a driver does not call on time to inform you that the vehicle has arrived, yet the park starts counting storage days against you. By the time you clear your bale, the profit is already gone.”

Similarly, Alhaja Rasheedat Suleiman, a palm oil and grain merchant, called on market associations and transport unions to intervene and establish fair, transparent guidelines.

“We understand that parks have limited space, but giving traders at least 48 hours of grace after proper notification is only fair,” Alhaja Suleiman said.

“Most of us are breadwinners supporting our families from these stalls. If transport companies and park unions do not regulate these charges, many women will be forced out of business.”

When contacted, a park supervisor at an interstate loading bay in, who declined to be named, defended the charges, stating that limited warehouse space and the risk of theft or damage make it necessary to compel traders to clear their goods promptly.

This growing extortion racket is more than a minor transport nuisance; it is an informal tax suffocating Nigeria’s micro and small enterprises.

Individuals are not left out of this ordeal

Mrs. Chidinma Okafor, a tailor, recounted her ordeal saying: “My sister sent me a small carton of clothes from Lagos and paid N4,000 at the park.

“When the driver called me, I was already waiting at the terminal. Yet, he refused to bring the bag down from the roof rack until I paid N3,500 for store room and park settlement.

“The bag never even touched the ground, let alone entered a store room.”

Ibrahim Jato, a baker, said: “I ordered baking ingredients from Onitsha for a weekend wedding cake, and the supplier already cleared the transport fare.”

“When I got to the park, three men surrounded the boot and demanded N8,000 for ‘store room security’ before releasing my items.

“ When I protested, the driver threatened to lock the boot and return with the goods the next day.

“I had no choice but to pay.”
